sourcedFrom: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) (UNDATED — nothing in the document states one)
cleanIntro: ⛔ Clean an Apex after every session or hunt — CVA is explicit that leaving corrosive powder in the bore even overnight invites damage that the warranty will not cover and that can make the gun unsafe. The long jag that came with the rifle turns the ramrod into a real cleaning rod; use it.

steps.title: ⛔ Read the serial number FIRST — CVA recalled a range of in-lines
steps.action: Before you clean, load or fire anything, read the serial number off the gun and look at how it ENDS. In August 1997 CVA recalled every in-line with a serial ending -95 or -96, and no catalog listing can tell you whether yours is one of them — only the number stamped on your gun can. If it ends that way, stop here and call CVA. Do not clean it, do not load it, and do not let anyone else use it.
steps.aside: If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line rifle with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use the gun under any circumstances.
steps.quote: In August of 1997, CVA implemented a Voluntary Recall of all in-line muzzleloading rifle models with serial numbers ending in –95 or –96.
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — VOLUNTARY RECALL

steps.title: Breech plug out, and the bore checked clear
steps.action: Before anything else, verify the rifle is unloaded and the bore is unobstructed by taking the breech plug out and looking through. On a muzzleloader this is the only honest chamber check there is.
steps.quote: Verify that your rifle is unloaded and the bore is unobstructed by removing the breech plug and looking through the bore.
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — LOADING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADING RIFLE

steps.title: ⛔ First patch WET WITH PLAIN WATER — it protects the finish
steps.action: Swab the bore several full strokes with a properly fitting wet patch, and make that FIRST patch plain water rather than solvent. CVA gives the reason on the page: it reduces the risk of staining the barrel. Follow with several dry patches.
steps.aside: Swab the bore several full strokes with a properly fitting wet patch.
steps.quote: To reduce the risk of staining your barrel we recommend this first patch to be wet with plain water.
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

steps.title: Breech plug out, wet with solvent, set aside
steps.action: Remove the breech plug, wet it thoroughly with cleaning solvent and set it aside to soak while you work on the bore.
steps.quote: Remove the breech plug, wet with cleaning solvent and set aside.
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

steps.title: Brush the bore, then patches until they come out clean
steps.action: Properly fitting bore brush on a cleaning rod to scrub the rifling and loosen the accumulated fouling, then several solvent-soaked patches to carry it out, then dry ones. Repeat the last two until the dry patches come out clean, then coat the bore with a rust-preventing gun oil.
steps.aside: Push several dry, clean patches through the bore.
steps.quote: Use a properly fitting bore brush on a cleaning rod to scrub the bore. This
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

steps.title: Plug: primer recess and flash hole, then grease FINGER TIGHT
steps.action: Wipe the plug with a solvent patch, and use cotton swabs and a wire nipple pick to clean the primer recess and the flash hole. ⛔ Then apply breech plug grease to the threads and install it finger tight — over-tightening will seize it.
steps.aside: Do not over tighten as this may cause the breechplug to seize.
steps.quote: Use cotton swabs and a wire nipple pick to clean the primer recess and flash hole. Apply breech plug grease to the threads and install finger tight.
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

steps.title: Breech face and a final wipe-down
steps.action: Patch and solvent around the firing pin on the breech face to take the primer residue off, then an oily rag or a rust-prevent patch over the whole exterior. Fouling left on the outside of a muzzleloader rusts it just as readily as fouling left inside.
steps.aside: Use an oily rag or a Rust Prevent Patch to wipe down the exterior of the gun to prevent rust and corrosion.
steps.quote: Use a patch and solvent to wipe the breech face around the firing pin to remove primer residue.
steps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Firing pin out with a 2.5 mm Allen — this one prevents a SLAM FIRE
deepSteps.action: After shooting blackpowder or a substitute, the firing pin and its hole must be cleaned. Take out the screw visible above the firing pin with a 2.5 mm Allen wrench and the pin and spring come out to the REAR. Clean the pin, the spring and the hole in the frame with solvent, oil them, and reassemble in reverse.
deepSteps.aside: Clean the firing pin, firing pin spring and the hole in the frame with solvent and oil.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 2.5mm allen wrench, remove the screw visible above the firing pin. The firing pin and spring will come out to the rear.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Then prove it travels AND retracts — the failure mode is a slam fire
deepSteps.action: Push on the firing pin to confirm it travels fully and smoothly, and verify it RETRACTS into the frame after being struck by the hammer. This is not a nicety. CVA spells out the consequence in capitals: a pin that is not properly maintained can fail to retract after firing, and the gun then fires involuntarily the next time it is loaded and closed.
deepSteps.aside: A FIRING PIN THAT IS NOT PROPERLY MAINTAINED CAN FAIL TO RETRACT AFTER FIRING RESULTING IN A "SLAM FIRE" CONDITION WHEREIN THE GUN FIRES INVOULENTARILY THE NEXT TIME IT IS LOADED AND CLOSED.
deepSteps.quote: Push on the firing pin to make sure it travels fully and smoothly. Verify that the pin retracts properly into the frame after being struck by the hammer.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Apex Owner's Manual — FORM 103C • Rev 1/11 (printed on the first page) — CLEANING YOUR CVA APEX MUZZLELOADER

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: ⛔ FIRST patch wet with PLAIN WATER — it stops the barrel staining
Dry patches, then a bore brush to loosen the fouling from the rifling
Solvent patches, then dry ones, repeated until they come out clean
Rust-preventing gun oil to coat the bore

cleaning.name: BREECH PLUG
tasks: Soaked in solvent while the bore is done, then wiped
⛔ Primer recess and flash hole cleared with swabs and a nipple pick
⛔ Threads greased, installed FINGER TIGHT — over-tight seizes it

cleaning.name: FIRING PIN (after every blackpowder session)
tasks: 2.5 mm Allen screw out; pin and spring come out to the REAR
Pin, spring and the hole in the frame cleaned with solvent, then oiled
⛔ Travel AND retraction proved — a pin that will not retract slam-fires

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Breech face wiped around the firing pin for primer residue
Oily rag or rust-prevent patch over the whole outside

reassembly: Firing pin and spring back in from the rear, 2.5 mm Allen screw refitted.
⛔ Breech plug threads greased, installed FINGER TIGHT only.
⛔ Firing pin travel and retraction proved before the rifle is loaded.
Exterior wiped with an oily rag or a rust-prevent patch.
fncheck: Reassembled: breech plug in finger tight with greased threads, firing pin screw back in. ⛔ Push the firing pin and confirm it travels fully and smoothly, then confirm it retracts into the frame after the hammer strikes it. If it does not retract, the rifle is not safe to load — that is the slam-fire condition CVA names. Then look through the bore from the breech end before anything is loaded.
